newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania monarchists vow daily rallies after vote.
newsitem.headline: Albania monarchists vow daily rallies after vote.

text.p: Hundreds of supporters of Albania's self-proclaimed king, some of them armed, gathered in central Tirana on Wednesday denouncing as falsified returns showing voters had rejected restoration of the monarchy.
Up to 300 monarchists denouncing the Socialist Party, apparent winners of Sunday's electon, disrupted traffic in central Skanderbeg Square at noon.
They dispersed only when an aide of King Leka I told them to hold daily rallies to demand revision of Sunday's referendum result, held alongside the general election.

"Let's come tomorrow at 12 o'clock in Tirana and stay together calmly and fearlessly until the restoration of the verdict of the people that the monarchy won," Abedin Mulosmani told the gathering. He said Leka would join his supporters.
A police minivan and an armoured personal carrier were stationed near the square but did not intervene. A government official at the site said no permission had been granted for such demonstrations.
Officials of Leka's "court" said he was spending the day in his villa close to the palace in a Tirana suburb used as a residence by his father, King Zog.

Leka said on Tuesday he had data showing between 54 percent and 65 percent of voters had backed the monarchy and accused the Socialists of mass manipulation. Partial returns, quoted by election officials on Wednesday, put support at 36 percent.

Leka I, who stands 2.04 metres (six feet 10 inches), fled Albania in 1939 ahead of an invasion by Italian Fascist troops when he was less than a week old. He has since lived in Spain, Britain and most recently in South Africa.
